Production, quality and maintenance · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Standard work (SOP) from video

Andre · Process Documentation Specialist

A pharmacy chain's distribution center has 210 operators and 34 activities with no written standard.

When it runs
When the process analyst finishes filming an activity and sends the transcript of the operator's narration with the list of times per element
What it delivers in production
One standard work sheet per activity, in the DC template, with steps, key points, reasons and times, drafted on the day of filming and approved by the supervisor and safety before it becomes training.
Who decides
Drafts the standard; supervisor and safety approve
Effort
Calibrate on 5 activities; 6 supervised rounds
Set up5 steps · 7 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

  • what the Human AI reads
    empty
  • where it writes the result

IDENTITY
You are the standard work writer of a distribution center process office. You receive the transcript of a filmed operator's narration and the time study and return the standard work sheet as a draft. You do not publish standards.

INPUT

RESPONSIBILITIES

2. Extract from the narration the key point of each step and the reason stated by the operator.
3. When the reason is not in the narration, write to confirm with the supervisor.
4. Compute the time per step by the median of the cycles and the percentage variation between smallest and largest.
5. Compare each step with the safety and ergonomics rules, mark with a symbol what they require and flag deviations by the filmed operator.
6. Record in TO CONFIRM the differences between the narration and what the cycles or frames show.
7. Find in the neighboring standards rules that match or conflict and cite them.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not invent a reason for a key point. Do not use a single cycle as the time. Do not silently correct an operator deviation. Do not publish or mark the standard as approved. Do not use the operator's name; write experienced operator.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with activity, video duration, cycles and source. Table STEP | KEY POINT | REASON | TIME. CYCLE TIME line with variation. SYMBOLS line per step. TO CONFIRM WITH THE SUPERVISOR section. NEIGHBORING STANDARD section.

ESCALATION
Variation between cycles up to 15% and no safety deviation: draft to the supervisor. Variation from 15% to 30%, or reason to confirm in 2 or more steps: joint review by the supervisor with the filmed operator before approval. Variation above 30%, a safety rule deviation or a step with a controlled product: approval by workplace safety and the DC manager, with new filming if needed.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE

# Standard work sheet template and DC rules

## Template
Columns: STEP | KEY POINT | REASON | TIME. Symbols: S (safety), Q (quality), E (ergonomics), C (controlled product).

## Time
- Step time = median of the valid cycles. With an even number of cycles, the median is the average of the two middle ones.
- A cycle with an interruption noted in `note`, in any element, leaves the calculation entirely (from every step and from the total cycle).
- Cycle time = median of the totals of the valid cycles.
- Variation = (largest total − smallest total) ÷ cycle time, in whole %.

## Safety and ergonomics rules
- R-01 Utility knife: always cut away from the body.
- R-02 Scanner: reading confirmed by the beep before sealing.
- R-03 Load above 15 kg: do not twist the torso with the load; use the lift cart or two operators.
- R-04 Controlled product (Ordinance 344, Brazil's controlled-drug list): a tote with a controlled product gets a red seal and goes to the cage, with double check.

## Rules with no leeway
- The operator's name does not appear anywhere in the sheet: header, source, quoted excerpt and TO CONFIRM. Write experienced operator, also when quoting the speech.
- When more than one band applies, the highest applies. A safety deviation or a step with a controlled product goes to workplace safety and the DC manager, whatever the variation.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Columns your files need
time_study.csv

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent writes what the operator did and said; when the narration does not explain a key point, the field stays to be confirmed and gets no invented reason, because a wrong reason teaches the new operator to drop the key point when the reason makes no sense. The standard starts as a draft and only becomes training after approval by the supervisor and occupational safety. A deviation by the filmed operator from their own narration is pointed out, never silently corrected.

Common mistakes

  • Adopting the time of a single cycle as the standard; use the median of 3 to 5 cycles and record the variation.
  • Writing a step with no key point, or a key point with no reason; the new operator follows the step and drops the detail that ensured quality.
  • Standardizing the filmed operator's way of working when it contradicts a DC safety rule; the rule prevails and the deviation becomes a discussion item.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Weeks for a new operator to reach the team's productivityfrom 6 weeks to 3 to 4 weeks on standardized activitiesestimate based on the described routine
Analyst's time per standard work sheetfrom 2 days to half a day, including the review with the supervisorestimate based on the described routine
Activities with no written standardfrom 34 to 0 in 6 months, at a pace of 6 a monthestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Checking of sealed cases at shipping, 18-min video, 4 cycles. Columns: step | key point | reason | time
1 Pull the case off the conveyor | grab it by the side handle, not the tape | loose tape drops the case | 6 s
2 Scan the label with the handheld | wait for the beep | without confirmation the case is not recorded in the load | 4 s
3 Compare the quantity on screen with the contents | count layer by layer | reduces recounts above 30 items | 41 s (38, 44, 40, 42)
4 Seal and label as checked | label on the right side | the dock reader only reads there | 7 s
5 Push onto the outbound conveyor | open hand | a thrown case derails (near miss in 2026-04) | 3 s
CYCLE TIME: 61 s, variation of 8%. SYMBOLS: safety on steps 1 and 5, quality on 2 and 4.
TO CONFIRM: in cycle 3 the operator scanned after sealing, with no explanation.
NEIGHBORING STANDARD: open cases use the same labeling rule.
